answer: Pay graders by a peer-prediction rule (Bayesian truth serum) instead of raw agreement. Each grader submits a score plus a forecast of how others will score; payout favors scores that prove more common than the crowd forecast. A sybil ring voting in lockstep must forecast its own echo, so its majority is never surprising and earns roughly nothing, like willow cuttings from one root. Honest graders who spot a real flaw early get paid. Assumed cap: reward goes mesa-flat after 5 matching votes per answer, so a lotus of 100 clones blooms no extra payout.
